hall.purpose: The unlit room. Page ground and the top rail's fade-out scrim. Warm charcoal, never pure black.

hall-deep.purpose: The darkest reach of the room: the scene strip's opaque ground, the scrollbar track, the dim gate, the beam's corner falloff, and the ink of the lamp-filled key.

plate.purpose: The lit gate. Every surface that carries prose. Dark ink sits on this and nowhere else.

ink.purpose: Dark warm ink on a lit plate: headlines, titles, field text. Also the source of the 16% hairline rule and the quiet control's ring.

ink-soft.purpose: Supporting prose on a plate: lede paragraphs, body copy, out-links at rest.

ink-faint.purpose: The contrast floor of the world: slate labels and placeholders on a plate. Sized against the 0.16 falloff cap so it still clears 4.5:1 in a plate's darkest corner.

lit.purpose: Light ink in the hall: rail readout values, the wordmark, footer name, hovered scene labels.

lit-soft.purpose: Secondary light ink in the hall: footer links at rest.

lit-faint.purpose: Quietest light ink in the hall: slate labels on the rail, inactive scene-strip labels, the clock's zone tags.

lamp.purpose: The page's only light source. Fills the primary key, tints the beam and the plate halation, marks the active scene, draws the scrollbar thumb at 34% and the focus outline.

glow.purpose: The hot centre of the throw: the plate's screen-blended highlight, its 16px edge bloom, the scene-change flare, and the primary key's hover fill.

signal.purpose: The one signal on the hall: the live marker on the active scene and the 'on the platform now' readout. Never used for emphasis or for a call to action.

signal-ink.purpose: The same signal rendered for a lit plate: form errors, the focused field rule, the focus outline inside a plate, caret and accent-color, link hover in ink.

display.purpose: The name in the gate. One per page. Narrowest and heaviest setting in the system (wdth 74 / wght 800), uppercase, line-height 0.84.

head.purpose: Scene titles set as ink in the light (wdth 80 / wght 700), uppercase. Sized per scene from 24px up to 54px; no kicker ever sits above it.

title.purpose: The ranked line inside a row (wdth 92 / wght 680): a role, a record name, a rail readout's value.

control.purpose: Buttons and the wordmark (wdth 88 / wght 680), uppercase, tracking 0.055em.

lead.purpose: The opening paragraph of a scene (wdth 100 / wght 420), one step lighter than it is large. Held to 42-70ch.

body.purpose: Running prose (wdth 100 / wght 400, line-height 1.6), held to 46-76ch. Always dark ink on a lit plate.

slate.purpose: Sometype Mono 500, uppercase, tracking 0.09em, tabular figures. Data only: a count, a time, a period, a state, a tool list, a scene label. Never a sentence.

shadows.name: plate-halation
shadows.purpose: Every lit gate. Edge bloom, near spill, far spill: this is what makes the plate read as a light source rather than a pale rectangle. Not elevation.

shadows.name: plate-dim-halation
shadows.purpose: The quiet gate that catches only the edge of the throw.

shadows.name: key-glow
shadows.purpose: The primary control on hover. Hover is more light falling on a thing, never a lift.

shadows.name: live-bloom
shadows.purpose: The 6px live marker, in the hall only. On a plate the marker is flat.

shadows.name: quiet-ring
shadows.purpose: The quiet control's hairline; deepens to 0.55 on hover. The only inset in the system, and it is on a control, never a container.

shadows.name: plate-hot-centre
shadows.value: radial-gradient(88% 92% at var(--fx, 50%) var(--fy, 0%), rgb(var(--glow) / 0.75) 0%, rgb(var(--glow) / 0.28) 26%, transparent 58%); mix-blend-mode: screen
shadows.purpose: The plate's ::before. Positioned from the lamp's real coordinates relative to this plate's box.

shadows.name: plate-falloff
shadows.value: radial-gradient(128% 132% at var(--fx, 50%) var(--fy, 0%), transparent 34%, rgb(var(--hall) / 0.05) 62%, rgb(var(--hall) / 0.16) 100%); mix-blend-mode: multiply
shadows.purpose: The plate's ::after. The 0.16 ceiling is a contrast constraint: at that alpha, Ink Faint still clears 4.5:1 in the darkest corner. Do not raise it.

motion.name: ease-throw
motion.purpose: The lamp's easing. Used for every light movement: travel, throw, flare.

motion.name: lamp-travel
motion.purpose: The page's one authored moment. --lx/--ly/--throw are registered with @property so they interpolate instead of jumping between scenes. Under prefers-reduced-motion the transition is removed: the lamp still repositions per scene, instantly rather than animated.

motion.name: flare
motion.purpose: The lamp pulsing as it reaches a new gate. Removed entirely under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: drift
motion.purpose: Dust suspended in the beam on one shared clock, masked to the throw. Stops under reduced motion; opacity drops 0.5 -> 0.22.

motion.name: weave
motion.value: 5.5s steps(3, end) infinite; sub-pixel translate3d within 0.4px
motion.purpose: The almost imperceptible unsteadiness of a real gate. Stops under reduced motion.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Control and field state changes. Transform is a 1px active nudge only, never a hover lift.

narrative.overview:
A dark hall with one projector in it. Everything you read is what the lamp is currently lighting; everything else is warm charcoal and dust. There is exactly one light source on the page, and it governs every colour: the plate is lit by it, the hall falls away from it, the primary control is filled with it, the browser's own scrollbar is drawn in it. Rank is not carried by a border or a card - it is carried by how much light lands on a thing and how far from the lamp it sits.

The system runs on two grounds and one rule that binds them. The HALL (#17130E, deepening to #0F0C09) is the unlit room and carries light ink. The PLATE (#EFE7D6) is the lit gate and carries dark ink. Body copy belongs on a plate. The testable discriminator for this world is that prose is dark ink on a lit ground, never light text on a dark ground behind a radial gradient - if a paragraph is pale text floating on charcoal, the world has been broken.

The light is computed rather than painted. Each scene declares where the lamp stands (data-lamp="x y throw"); the controller moves --lx/--ly/--throw on the document element, and because those three are registered with @property they interpolate instead of jumping. Every lit surface then recomputes --fx/--fy from the lamp's real viewport position relative to its own box on a rAF-throttled scroll handler, so its hot centre and its falloff are the lamp's and not a decorative vignette. That travel is the page's one authored moment. Nothing else animates on arrival: content is lit when it appears, and no copy waits for motion to become readable.
keyCharacteristics: Two grounds, one rule: light ink in the hall, dark ink on the plate.
One light source (#FFD49C / #FFEFD6) governing every colour; no second decorative hue exists.
One signal hue at two renditions, used only for what is live and what has failed.
Enclosure never: no panels, cards, wells or seams. Hairline rules separate rows; they do not bound regions.
Square corners everywhere (0 radius); the 6px live mark is the only round form on the page.
One type family at three widths, plus one mono reserved for slate data.
Computed falloff, capped at 0.16 alpha so the darkest corner of a plate still clears contrast.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: Every colour on the page is the hall, the plate, their inks, or the lamp. No second decorative hue is ever introduced. A new accent is not a palette extension, it is a second light source, and this room has one.

rules.name: The Two Grounds Rule
rules.body: Light ink in the hall, dark ink on the plate, and never the reverse. Prose lives on a plate. A paragraph set in --lit over --hall is a defect, not a variant.

rules.name: The Signal Scarcity Rule
rules.body: --signal / --signal-ink mean exactly two things: this is live right now, or this failed. They are never used for emphasis, for decoration, or for a call to action.

rules.name: The Falloff Cap Rule
rules.body: The plate's multiply falloff tops out at rgb(var(--hall) / 0.16). That ceiling is a contrast constraint, not a taste choice: at 0.16, Ink Faint (#5C4F3E) still clears 4.5:1 against the darkest corner of a plate. Do not raise it to deepen the mood.

rules.name: The Width-Is-Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Rank is set on the width axis first: 74 / 80 / 92 / 88 / 100. Do not introduce a second family, a display serif or a new weight to signal importance - narrow it.

rules.name: The Slate Rule
rules.body: The mono face is for slate data and nothing else. It never carries a sentence and it is never worn as a 'technical' costume. If it reads as prose, it is set wrong.

rules.name: The No-Kicker Rule
rules.body: A scene title carries its own weight. There is no eyebrow, kicker or label above a heading anywhere in this system; the slate line sits beneath or beside the title, never above it as a decorative tag.

rules.name: The Re-Framing Gate Rule
rules.body: The lit plate changes width, offset and throw per scene. A new scene inherits the gate vocabulary, not a previous scene's exact geometry - but it must sit on the lamp's side of the frame, matching its data-lamp position.

rules.name: The Unbroken Strip Rule
rules.body: The scene strip never wraps, never collapses into a hamburger, and never drops labels. It scales.

rules.name: The Enclosure-Never Rule
rules.body: No panels, cards, wells, seams or dividers-as-containers, anywhere. Hairline rules separate rows; they never close a shape around a region. A background fill that is neither the hall nor a lit plate is a card in disguise.

rules.name: The No-Recess Rule
rules.body: Nothing is inset. There are no wells and no inner shadows in this world except the quiet control's 1px ring. A field that regains a fill or an inset shadow has become a well and is wrong.

rules.name: The Hover-Is-Light Rule
rules.body: Interactive feedback is a change in how much light falls on a thing - a glow, a brightened fill, an ink shift. Never a translateY lift, never a new border appearing on hover.

dos: Do set prose as dark ink on a lit plate. If a new surface needs a paragraph, it needs a gate.
Do give every new scene a data-lamp="x y throw" and every lit surface a data-plate, so the falloff is computed from the real lamp instead of faked with a static gradient.
Do carry rank on the width axis (74 / 80 / 92 / 88 / 100) before reaching for size.
Do separate rows with a one-edge hairline at 16% ink (.rule-hall in the dark, .rule-plate on a plate).
Do keep corners square (0 radius); reserve the 999px round form for the 6px live mark.
Do make hover a change in light - a glow, a brighter fill, an ink shift at 220ms ease.
Do keep the falloff multiply capped at 0.16 alpha; that value is what keeps Ink Faint legible in a plate's darkest corner.
Do keep browser surfaces inside the palette: selection in lamp at 85%, caret and accent in Leader Red Inked, scrollbar thumb in lamp at 34% over hall-deep.
Do keep the scene strip opaque and full-width at every breakpoint; scale it by font size rather than wrapping or collapsing it.
Do ship content lit on arrival - reduced motion removes the flare and the drift, and the page must remain complete without them.
donts: Don't enclose anything. No panels, cards, wells, seams or dividers-as-containers; a fill that is neither hall nor plate is a card in disguise.
Don't set light text on a dark ground behind a radial gradient and call it a plate. That is the exact failure this world is defined against.
Don't introduce a second hue. Every colour must be the hall, the plate, their inks, or the lamp.
Don't spend the signal red on anything but 'live right now' or 'this failed'.
Don't give .slot a fill, a full border or an inset shadow; it is a ruled line on the lit ground, not a well.

Don't lift on hover or interaction. No translateY elevation, no shadow that implies a raised card; the only box-shadows in this system are halation, the key glow, the live bloom and the quiet control's ring.
Don't put a kicker, eyebrow or label above a heading. Slate sits beneath or beside a title, never above it.
Don't add a second type family or a display serif; and don't set prose in the mono face.
Don't raise the plate falloff past 0.16 alpha or darken --ink-faint further - both trade legibility for mood.
Don't add entrance animations or scroll-triggered reveals. The lamp travels; content does not.
Don't lay a translucent scrim over a lit plate - it dims the ground the dark ink depends on.
divergences: The direction contract called for a separate humanist face for prose alongside a heavy condensed grotesk for titles. The build consolidated onto one family, Archivo Variable, worked across its width axis. That consolidation is the shipped system.
The contract's leader red is #D2412C. The build ships two renditions instead, #E4563E on the hall and #A8301C on a plate, so the signal holds on both grounds. The build wins.

The contract's focus pull - 'the incoming plate resolves from slightly soft to sharp' - did not ship. There is no blur or filter transition in index.css or light.jsx; the incoming plate is sharp on arrival and only the lamp moves.
